mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI OM668 engine typically costs £950-£1,550 supply-only, depending on power output (75hp or 91hp) and supplier. Used units start from £450. Supply & fit adds £450-£750 labour. Prices vary by condition and supplier location.

mainEntity.name: What engine code does my Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI have?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI uses the OM668 DE1.6 LA engine, also known as 668.914 (ME2). This 1.7-litre common-rail diesel was fitted to all Vaneo 1.7 CDI variants from 2001 to 2005. Verify via your V5C logbook, VIN plate, or by entering your registration on our compatibility checker.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of EGR valve failure on a Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: EGR valve failure on the Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI typically presents as excessive black smoke from the exhaust, loss of power under acceleration, rough idle, and limp mode activation. Fault codes P1403 (EGR vacuum transducer) and P1470 (charge pressure control) are common.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is in good condition and the replacement cost stays below the vehicle's value. With Vaneo values typically £800-£2,500, a rebuilt engine at £950-£1,550 plus fitting represents a significant investment - carefully assess body condition, mileage and MOT history.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI OM668 engine regularly exceeds 200,000 miles. One owner reported 360,000 km (224,000 miles) with no major engine problems. Regular oil changes, EGR valve cleaning and timely injector seal replacement are essential for longevity.

mainEntity.name: Are Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI engines interchangeable with A-Class W168?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI shares the OM668 engine with the W168 A-Class, but mount points, wiring harnesses and ECU calibrations differ. Always verify chassis-specific compatibility before ordering a replacement unit. The Vaneo uses engine code 668.914 while the A-Class uses 668.940 variants.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz Vaneo 1.7 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes Benz Vaneo 1.7 CDI launched in 2001 as the diesel workhorse of the W414 platform - a compact MPV/van hybrid that shared its engine architecture with the W168 A-Class. Powered by the OM668 DE1.6 LA 1.7-litre common-rail diesel, the 1.7 CDI offered strong low-end torque and excellent fuel economy for urban commercial and family use. Production ran from 2001 to 2005, with two power outputs - 75hp and 91hp - across Trend, Ambiente, Family and Commercial trims.

milestones.description: **2001** - Vaneo 1.7 CDI launched with OM668 DE1.6 LA 75hp (55kW) and 91hp (67kW) variants
**2003** - Peak UK sales year; EGR valve revisions introduced (A6681410060)
**2004** - Late-production OM668 units receive updated injector calibration
**2005** - Final production year; Vaneo discontinued with no direct successor

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI's OM668 engine is generally robust and durable for its era - one owner reported 360,000 km (224,000 miles) with no major engine problems. However, the combination of EGR system clogging, turbo actuator wear and injector seal failure creates distinct failure patterns that drive UK replacement enquiries. Every rebuilt OM668 engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: EGR Valve Clogging - Why Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI Engines Lose Power and Smoke Excessively
problems.rootCause: Carbon-heavy exhaust gases recirculate directly into the intake manifold without a modern DPF to filter soot, causing rapid valve sticking and restricted airflow. Owners report mass amounts of smoke from the exhaust, particularly on take-off and under high revs. The valve's plunger becomes thick with black, gummy oil. Fault codes P1403 (EGR vacuum transducer) and P1470 (charge pressure control) are common.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removal of EGR valve, manual decarbonisation with carburettor cleaner, vacuum hose inspection and lubrication
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; may need repeating if root cause (vacuum leak) not addressed

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - EGR Valve Replacement & Intake Clean
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removal of clogged EGR valve, replacement with updated unit (A6681410060), professional carbon cleaning of intake runners
repairOptions.longevity: Restores power; addresses the root cause permanently

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of bench-tested rebuilt OM668 unit with pre-cleaned intake ports, new EGR valve, and 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary only if severe EGR failure has caused hydrolock or excessive cylinder wall scoring

problems.recommendation: The OM668 responds well to a standalone EGR valve replacement and intake strip-down. We recommend this route for most budget-conscious owners unless diagnostic tests confirm deep internal scoring or coolant ingress. A simple clean of the EGR valve and checking for kinked vacuum hoses can resolve many smoking issues.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM668 diesel engine prices for your Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI

problems.h4: Turbo Actuator Failure - Why Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI Engines Enter Limp Mode
problems.rootCause: The turbocharger's pneumatic wastegate actuator diaphragm degrades under sustained heat cycles, causing boost pressure leaks, erratic vane positioning, and ECU limp-mode activation. Symptoms include stalling during deceleration, RPM limiting above 3,500 rpm, and loss of power. The turbo's or EGR's vacuum control valves may be leaking vacuum.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Turbo extraction, installation of reinforced actuator diaphragm and silicone boost hoses, ECU reset
repairOptions.longevity: Restores boost control effectively; does not address underlying turbo bearing wear

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt OM668 Engine with New Turbo
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of bench-tested rebuilt OM668 with new turbo assembly, reinforced actuator, and 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best choice if turbo shaft play or blade damage has already occurred; guarantees consistent boost performance

problems.recommendation: Replacing just the actuator is a cost-effective first step for a Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI showing intermittent boost loss. However, if metallic scraping is audible or black soot is present around the turbo housing, a full rebuilt engine with a fresh turbo core is the only reliable long-term fix. Check the wastegate actuator rod retention clip - a missing clip is a known cause of actuator disconnection.
problems.cta: -> Compare Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI rebuilt engine prices now

problems.h4: Injector Seal Failure - Why Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI Engines Lose Compression and Sound Rough
problems.rootCause: Injector seals degrade over time, allowing combustion gases to escape past the injector. Owners report a "Phhhew" sound every 4th stroke, along with smoke and smell in the engine compartment. Injector seats on the cylinder head need to be re-cut; without this, new seals will leak again.

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Injector Seal Replacement & Seat Recut
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removal of injectors, recutting of injector seats, new seals and stretch bolts
Supply & fit of rebuilt OM668 with new injectors, seals and cylinder head work
repairOptions.longevity: Only necessary if injector failure has caused cylinder head damage

problems.recommendation: Injector seal failure is a common and relatively inexpensive fix on the OM668. A competent specialist can replace seals and recut seats in around four hours. If the vehicle has a history of multiple injector failures or the head is damaged, a rebuilt engine may be more cost-effective.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM668 Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI Engines Rattle on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The OM668 uses a chain-driven double overhead camshaft arrangement. The timing chain tensioner can wear over time, causing chain slack and a rattling noise on cold starts. The intake camshaft is driven via a single roller chain, with the exhaust camshaft driven via gearwheel engagement.

repairOptions.longevity: Recommended at first sign of cold-start rattle; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Only necessary if chain has jumped or caused valve damage

problems.recommendation: Do not ignore a cold-start rattle on your Mercedes Vaneo 1.7 CDI. A timing chain kit replacement is significantly cheaper than repairing a bent-valve OM668 engine. Many Vaneo 1.7 CDI owners have reported 360,000 km (224,000 miles) without engine problems - but chain tensioner wear is the main exception.
